stories.title: RRB increases Junior Engineer vacancies
stories.summary: The Railway Recruitment Board has released the provisional answer key for its Junior Engineer CBT-1 exam. The board increased the total number of available posts by 458, bringing the final count to 4,487 vacancies. Candidates may now compare their responses against the newly published key.

stories.summary: IIT Madras has opened the correction window for GATE 2027 application forms. Candidates can rectify errors regarding their name, date of birth, exam city, or paper code until November 14. The window is available for those who have already submitted their applications.

stories.title: 8th Pay Commission report timeline remains uncertain
stories.summary: Central government employees may wait until 2027 for the Eighth Pay Commission to finalise recommendations on salaries and pensions. Although the Commission marked its first year on November 3, 2026, the government has allowed 18 months from its constitution for the final report to be submitted.

stories.title: Cabinet approves museum and transport projects
stories.summary: The Union Cabinet approved the development of the Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum in New Delhi for ₹3,230 crore. Other decisions include extending the Noida Metro Aqua Line and setting fertiliser subsidy rates for the Rabi 2026-27 season. The government continues to manage its infrastructure and agricultural priorities.

stories.title: Maruti Suzuki dominates October car sales
stories.summary: Maruti Suzuki models occupied seven of the top ten spots in October 2026, with the Wagon R leading at 23,747 units. Total sales for the top ten models rose 17.41 percent year on year. Maruti’s Brezza saw an 85.85 percent increase in sales compared to last October.

stories.title: Electric vehicle sales grow 76 percent in October
stories.summary: Electric passenger vehicle retail sales reached 37,049 units in October 2026, a 76.47 percent increase from the previous year. Tata Passenger Electric Mobility remains the market leader, followed by Mahindra and JSW MG Motor India. The segment's total market share fell compared to September.

stories.title: Honda Elevate sales rise in October
stories.summary: Honda sold 3,673 units of the Elevate in October, marking a 68 percent annual increase. The Amaze followed with 3,337 units, though it recorded an 8.1 percent annual decline. The company continues to monitor the performance of its remaining models.

stories.title: Maruti Suzuki Dzire dominates sedan segment
stories.summary: The Maruti Suzuki Dzire recorded 20,649 wholesale dispatches in October, capturing 49.4 percent of the ten-entry sedan market. Tata Aeris sales reached 4,005 units following the discontinuation of the Tigor. Total segment dispatches rose 12.3 percent compared to the previous year. These figures represent dealer shipments, not retail sales.

stories.title: Wagon R becomes India's best-selling car
stories.summary: Maruti Suzuki's Wagon R reached the top of the sales chart in October with 23,747 units dispatched. The model moved from fifth place in September to the number one spot in October. The performance highlights a sustained demand for affordable family hatchbacks in the current market.

stories.title: Mahindra Vision S spotted during testing
stories.summary: Two test mules of the upcoming Mahindra Vision S compact SUV were sighted in Hyderabad. Spy shots reveal an upright design, six vertical grille slots, and rear pillar lights reminiscent of the Scorpio. The company has yet to confirm official specifications or a launch date for the vehicle.

stories.summary: A new seven-seater vehicle has been spotted during road testing. The full details regarding the manufacturer and technical specifications remain unavailable, as the project is currently in the pre-launch phase. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: Next-generation Hyundai Creta interior revealed
stories.summary: The third-generation Hyundai Creta has been sighted testing in Manali, revealing a redesigned dashboard, larger infotainment screen, and slim digital display. The model is expected to launch by mid-2027, featuring a new strong-hybrid petrol engine and an increased footprint based on the Seltos K3 platform.

stories.summary: VIDA has unveiled the UBX concept at EICMA 2026, marking the brand's first foray into electric motorcycles. The concept features neo-naked styling, a TFT display, and upside-down forks. The company has not confirmed production plans, launch timing, or technical specifications for the new model.

stories.title: Royal Enfield Hunter 350 and Classic 350 compared
stories.summary: The Hunter 350 and Classic 350 share a 349cc engine producing 20.2bhp and 27Nm. While the mechanical foundations are identical, the models differ in styling and ergonomics. The Hunter is marketed for city navigation, while the Classic retains the brand's traditional aesthetic for different buyer preferences.

stories.title: Royal Enfield Himalayan 750 debut scheduled
stories.summary: Royal Enfield will showcase the Himalayan 750 at EICMA 2026, featuring a 750cc parallel-twin engine. The motorcycle is expected to cost approximately Rs 4.50 lakh and will be launched in India at Motoverse in late November. It will sit at the top of the brand's current engine lineup.

stories.title: L5 electric auto sales overtake e-rickshaws
stories.summary: L5 electric auto sales reached 1,28,010 units in Q2 FY27, a 122 percent increase year-on-year. Meanwhile, e-rickshaw sales fell 16 percent to 93,036 units. The passenger market has shifted, with L5 models now outselling the traditional L3 e-rickshaw segment by roughly 35,000 units.

stories.title: BGauss crosses 1 lakh cumulative sales
stories.summary: BGauss has delivered 1,00,595 electric scooters since August 2022. Sales in 2026 reached 41,849 units, a 104 percent increase over the same period last year. The company has maintained a position in the top ten electric two-wheeler brands for every month of the current year.

stories.title: TVS Motor expands global scooter portfolio
stories.summary: TVS Motor has launched the Callisto 110 scooter in the Turkish market. The expansion is part of the company's ongoing strategy to increase its global footprint. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: Exicom CEO forecasts charger demand
stories.summary: Exicom CEO Anant Nahata estimates India will require 25,000 additional DC fast chargers over the next three years. The projection accounts for 60 to 80 percent annual growth in electric passenger vehicle sales, alongside the induction of electric buses and trucks into the national fleet.

stories.title: Oben Electric leads e-motorcycle sales
stories.summary: Oben Electric recorded 1,565 e-motorcycle sales in October 2026, surpassing Revolt Intellicorp. Oben's sales grew 4.2x between January and October. Revolt Intellicorp maintains the highest total sales for the first ten months of the year, with 9,842 units delivered. These figures exclude Ola Electric.

stories.title: Annual electric vehicle sales exceed 3 lakh
stories.summary: Retail sales of electric passenger vehicles reached 3,04,701 units between January 1 and November 9, 2026. This represents a 66 percent year-on-year growth and exceeds the total sales for the entirety of 2025 by 56 percent. The segment continues to show consistent monthly growth.

stories.summary: The International Energy Agency reports that over 20 million plug-in cars were sold globally last year. While the U.S. electric vehicle market faces stagnation, the report notes that the project is chugging along nicely elsewhere. The U.S. is increasingly the odd one out.

stories.summary: Used electric vehicle prices rose two percent in October, while petrol and diesel values fell. Data from Cazana shows electric prices are 4.7 percent higher than at the start of the year and 11 percent higher than this time last year. Used cars are bucking the trend.

stories.title: Used electric vehicle sales hit record high in March
stories.summary: Americans bought 42,924 used electric vehicles in March, setting a new monthly record according to Cox Automotive. Sales rose 28 percent year over year, even as new electric vehicle sales slumped by a similar amount. The secondhand market is shrugging off the tax credit hangover.

stories.title: Electric vehicles displaced 2.3 million barrels of oil daily in 2025
stories.summary: Electric vehicles and plug-in hybrids displaced 2.3 million barrels of oil per day in 2025, according to BloombergNEF. The company projects this figure will more than double by the end of the decade as sales continue to climb. The future of diesel is not looking great.

stories.summary: The government has extended its climate bonus for electric vehicles and charging infrastructure through mid-2030. A pre-financing mechanism will launch on 1 January 2027. stories.title: Mexico heavy-duty vehicle production surges in October
stories.summary: Mexico produced 16,375 heavy-duty vehicles in October, a 129.6 percent increase over the 7,131 units manufactured in October 2025. The industry achieved this milestone even as broader automotive manufacturing corridors navigated retooling pauses and trade headwinds. The growth is described as explosive.

stories.title: Electric van registrations increase in the EU
stories.summary: European registrations for externally chargeable vans reached 151,691 in the first nine months of the year, a 38.2 percent increase compared to the previous year. While overall van registrations remained flat, the market for chargeable drivetrains showed growth. The figures come from the European Automobile Manufacturers Association.

stories.title: BYD commercial vehicle sales rise 68 percent in October
stories.summary: BYD sold 600 electric buses in October, a 62.1 percent increase compared to October 2025. While year-over-year figures rose, sales were down 24.1 percent compared to September 2026. The company continues to publish its monthly reports on passenger and commercial vehicle sales.

stories.title: Nigeria targets 500,000 annual vehicle production
stories.summary: The National Automotive Design and Development Council says Nigeria has the capacity to produce 500,000 vehicles annually. Director-General Joseph Osanipin stated that domestic demand is up to 450,000 units, provided the industry receives stronger financing and policy support. The country is currently working to realise that potential.

stories.title: KTM X-Bow Arrow revealed as 330hp Dakar-inspired off-roader
stories.summary: KTM X-Bow has unveiled the Arrow, a side-by-side off-roader developed with input from Dakar rally-raid competitors. The project was initiated by owner and rally driver Guillaume de Mévius, whose G Rally Team served as the development platform. Reservations open on November 17 through the brand's dealer network.

stories.title: Queen Creek shop supports women in automotive careers
stories.summary: APA Total Car Care is backing Amazing Women in Automotive, an organization focused on recruiting and mentoring female professionals. Owner Sean Gordon says the support reflects a belief that women should have clear pathways to lead within the industry. The shop is currently women-led.

stories.title: South Korean auto parts makers plan investment in Tamil Nadu
stories.summary: Hwashin Automotive India and Seoyon E-Hwa Summit have proposed a combined investment of Rs 1,370 crore in Tamil Nadu over the next five years. Hwashin plans to spend Rs 850 crore on research, manufacturing technologies, and capacity enhancement. The companies confirmed the plans in letters dated November 11.

stories.title: South Korean auto components firms commit Rs 1,370 crore to Tamil Nadu
stories.summary: Hwashin Automotive and Seoyon E-Hwa Summit have pledged Rs 1,370 crore in investments over five years, countering reports that suppliers were shifting manufacturing to Andhra Pradesh. The companies confirmed the commitment in formal letters to the Tamil Nadu government on November 11.

stories.title: Talbros Automotive reports record revenue in Q2
stories.summary: Talbros Automotive recorded net sales of ₹263.21 crores in Q2 FY27, the highest in company history. Operating margins contracted to 16.31% from 17.28% due to rising input costs. The company says it is well-positioned to capitalise on the recovering automotive market despite the margin pressure.

stories.title: Talbros Automotive reports profit surge
stories.summary: Talbros Automotive Components reported a 43.2% year-on-year net profit increase to ₹32.94 crore for Q2. The company holds multi-year orders exceeding ₹1,000 crore. Shares closed at Rs 415.50 on Wednesday, up 6.72 percent from the previous close. Carmakers test and approve parts long before vehicles launch.

stories.title: Apollo Tyres reports profit growth
stories.summary: Apollo Tyres reported a 13.2% year-on-year increase in consolidated net profit to ₹2,922.87 million for the quarter ended September 30. Revenue rose 16.6% to ₹79,681.50 million, driven by the APMEA segment. Citi maintained a Buy rating, noting that Indian results offset weak performance in the European business.

stories.title: Balkrishna Industries to launch passenger car tyres
stories.summary: Balkrishna Industries aims to launch its own passenger car tyres in the Indian replacement market in January 2027. The company intends to gradually build up branded volumes following the pilot. Senior president Satish Sharma confirms that a network of distributors is already in place for the new line.

stories.title: Exide showcases battery lineup in Dubai
stories.summary: Exide is showcasing its automotive battery lineup at Automechanika Dubai. The event features manufacturers and suppliers from the global aftermarket, focusing on trends in service, repair, and new technologies. The company is highlighting its current range of products for the automotive sector.

stories.title: Supplier Martinrea teams with Raytheon on missile production
stories.summary: The full piece is for subscribers. Martinrea International has announced a working relationship between its subsidiary, TruNorth Aerospace and Defense, and Raytheon to help accelerate Tomahawk cruise missile production. The supplier is applying its factory playbook to the defence sector.

stories.title: Martinrea brings auto-plant know-how to Raytheon
stories.summary: Martinrea International has established a working relationship with Raytheon to accelerate Tomahawk cruise missile production. The company is using its subsidiary, TruNorth Aerospace and Defense, to apply automotive factory playbooks to the defence line. It is another Canadian auto manufacturer stepping into the defence manufacturing sector.

stories.title: Stackpole releases resistors for automotive electronics
stories.summary: Stackpole has introduced its RPCQ series of automotive-grade chip resistors designed for compact, power-dense electronics. The components are intended to protect circuits from electrical transients in EV power management and battery systems. The company claims the series combines pulse handling capability with long-term stability.

stories.title: Visteon-Shinry and Infineon develop GaN onboard charger
stories.summary: The full piece is for subscribers. Visteon-Shinry and Infineon have collaborated to develop a gallium nitride onboard charger. The project focuses on integrating advanced power electronics for automotive applications. Further details regarding the technical specifications and production timeline remain unavailable.

stories.title: Auto suppliers seek cost recovery
stories.summary: The full piece is for subscribers. Automotive suppliers are intensifying efforts to recover costs as inflation impacts manufacturing margins. Companies are seeking savings across the supply chain to manage rising input prices and competitive pressures in the current market environment.

stories.title: FTC reaches agreement with Long Island car dealer
stories.summary: The FTC reached an agreement with Stream Auto Outlet over allegations that the dealer misled consumers with online pricing. The government alleges the dealership buried down payments and fees in fine print. The court order requires the dealer to prominently display the actual price a consumer must pay.

stories.title: Anderson Automotive Group acquires Florida dealerships
stories.summary: Anderson Automotive Group has acquired Acura of Fort Myers and Lexus of Fort Myers from Group 1 Automotive. The dealerships will continue operations at their South Tamiami Trail locations. The Presidio Group served as the exclusive buy-side advisor for the transaction, which was announced October 26.

stories.title: North Olmsted car dealer goes viral
stories.summary: The full piece is for subscribers. A car dealership in North Olmsted has gained social media attention for its branding efforts. The dealership's marketing approach has reportedly gone viral across various platforms, drawing interest to its specific brand identity and online presence.

stories.title: RockED and Hendrick Automotive Group partner on training
stories.summary: RockED has announced a nationwide partnership with Hendrick Automotive Group to implement its AI-powered learning platform. The collaboration aims to transform dealership performance through short-form training modules. Hendrick has been following the company's growth since 2022 and previously adopted the platform through various OEM programs.

stories.title: Helion Technologies launches managed AI for dealerships
stories.summary: Helion Technologies has introduced Helion Managed AI, a platform designed to replace unsupervised consumer AI tools at automotive dealerships. The company says the service provides governed access to generative AI for staff across sales and finance. Dealership employees have been using consumer chat tools on personal devices.

stories.title: Drive Motor Retail unveils new Vauxhall showroom
stories.summary: Drive Darlington has adopted Vauxhall’s latest corporate identity as part of a multimillion-pound redevelopment. The site now hosts six Stellantis brands across 1,000 square meters of showroom space. The facility includes 18 workshop bays and 13 electric vehicle charging points to accommodate the expanded sales and aftersales operations.

stories.title: Hendy Automotive confirms Simon Bottomley as COO
stories.summary: Hendy Automotive has appointed Simon Bottomley as chief operating officer following the departure of Duncan McPhee. Bottomley previously held the role at the retailer between 2018 and 2023. His return was confirmed via Companies House filings shortly after the termination of McPhee’s directorship was announced.

stories.title: JLR dealers face showroom cost pressures
stories.summary: Former dealer boss Daksh Gupta has warned that Jaguar Land Rover retailers face challenges covering the costs of expensive showroom facilities. As Jaguar shifts toward a lower-volume electric strategy, fewer vehicles are expected to pass through premises originally designed to accommodate both Jaguar and Land Rover brands.

stories.title: Motorpoint targets 120,000 annual sales
stories.summary: Motorpoint plans to expand its network to 35 dealerships to support a target of 120,000 annual vehicle sales. The group reported an 80.6 percent rise in half-year pre-tax profit. While the company is closing its Ipswich site, it says the new Leeds location is trading ahead of plan.

stories.title: Eastern Western reaches 2MW solar milestone across dealerships
stories.summary: Eastern Western Motor Group has reached a two megawatt solar capacity across its facilities. The two-year programme involved installations at 19 sites, including luxury showrooms in Newbridge. The group expects the panels to generate 1.66 million kWh of electricity annually. The sun remains a consistent, if seasonal, partner.

stories.title: SDV cybersecurity risks a top fear of developers
stories.summary: Automotive developers rank cybersecurity risks for software-defined vehicles among their primary concerns, according to a QNX survey of 1,100 embedded software engineers. While respondents reported high confidence in their productivity and compliance capabilities, the industry remains wary of external threats. Security is now a feature, not a bug.

stories.title: Five ways OEMs are using AI in vehicles
stories.summary: Artificial intelligence is increasingly integrated into modern vehicle development and fleet management. OEMs are deploying the technology for telematics, safety features, and voice assistants. As software-defined vehicles become the industry standard, manufacturers are finding that technology is now a priority. The car is becoming a computer that occasionally moves.

stories.title: Dongfeng Stellantis and Volcano Engine partner on AI cockpits
stories.summary: Dongfeng Stellantis Automotive Technology and Volcano Engine have signed a strategic agreement to develop intelligent cockpit systems. The partnership includes joint research into on-device AI and system-on-chip planning. DSAT will be the first joint-venture automaker to adopt the company's AI cockpit assistant. Intelligence is now a standard interior trim.

stories.title: Pakistan targets $6bn in auto exports by 2031
stories.summary: Pakistan has introduced a new automotive policy targeting $6 billion in exports by 2031. The plan includes binding localisation requirements and a Rs2.1 billion vendor upgrade programme to shift the industry toward export-oriented manufacturing. The government aims to reduce dependence on imported components through domestic production mandates.

stories.title: Carmakers urge energy secretary to relax electric vehicle targets
stories.summary: The full piece is for subscribers. Carmakers are reportedly lobbying the UK government to ease electric vehicle sales targets. The current requirements have faced pushback from manufacturers citing market challenges. The energy secretary is expected to review the policy amid ongoing industry pressure.

stories.title: Labour MPs warn against weakening electric vehicle targets
stories.summary: Labour MPs are urging the government to maintain the legal requirement for 80% of new car sales to be electric by 2030. Cabinet ministers are scheduled to meet Thursday to discuss potential compromises. Proponents argue that weakening the target would be a shortsighted step for the industry.

stories.title: UK may cut 2030 EV sales target to 60%
stories.summary: The UK government is considering reducing its 2030 zero-emission vehicle sales target from 80% to 60% while extending compliance flexibilities until 2034. Battery-electric vehicles accounted for 26.6% of sales through October, missing the 33% target. The gap between ambition and the showroom floor remains wide.

stories.title: Philippine auto industry warns of luxury tax impact
stories.summary: The Philippine auto industry has warned that a proposed 75 percent tax on luxury vehicles could negatively affect sales and revenues. The industry group suggests the high levy may deter buyers, potentially impacting the broader automotive market in the region.

stories.title: Ukraine introduces 183-day rule for car sales
stories.summary: Ukraine has passed law No. 16037-d, requiring owners to pay 18 percent income tax on car sales if the vehicle was held for less than 183 days. This applies even to a first sale within a year, excluding additional military taxes. Quick sales are now officially discouraged.

stories.title: Government mandates electric vehicles for staff fleets
stories.summary: The Indian government has made electric vehicles the default choice for staff-car procurement, raising the price ceiling to Rs 20 lakh from the previous Rs 10 lakh limit for combustion engines. Shares of several electric vehicle companies rose following the announcement of the new expenditure policy.

stories.title: Government consults on electric vehicle charging
stories.summary: The government has released two consultations regarding electric vehicle infrastructure. One seeks to expand charging access for residential tenants and leaseholders, while the other proposes amendments to Building Regulations Part S. The National Housing Federation plans to respond to the proposals before the 16 December deadline.

stories.title: Democrats weigh reversal of auto industry policies
stories.summary: Following two years of Republican regulatory and tax changes, newly empowered Democrats may attempt to reverse several Trump administration policies affecting the American auto industry. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: India targets Formula One return by 2027
stories.summary: Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya stated that preparations are underway for Formula One to return to India before 2027, following a 13-year absence. The minister noted that track-related issues have been resolved, with work expected to conclude within six months to meet the hosting goal.

stories.title: Winners crowned at F1 Sim Racing India Open
stories.summary: The inaugural F1 Sim Racing India Open concluded at Mumbai’s NSCI Dome. Vihaan Joshi won the Junior title, while Karl Verghese secured the Senior title. The event, organised by Mumbai Falcons, serves as a qualifier for the team's karting programme, with Season 2 registrations opening 19 November.

stories.title: Team Spain White wins Cup of Nations in Mumbai
stories.summary: Team Spain White won the Cup of Nations title in Mumbai, defeating 20 international teams. Led by Ismael Fahssi, the team secured victory after three days of competition. The event was organised by Mumbai Falcons Racing Limited in partnership with Formula 1, featuring international sim racing drivers.

stories.title: International riders join Indian Supercross League
stories.summary: The Indian Supercross Racing League has concluded its Season 3 riders auction, attracting international talent from the United States, Australia, Europe, and Asia. The franchise-based platform selected 13 riders across teams, reflecting the growing professional interest in the sport within the Indian market.

stories.title: India launches first hydrogen-powered train
stories.summary: India has inaugurated its first indigenous hydrogen fuel cell-powered train. The locomotive generates electricity onboard and is scheduled to operate on the Jind-Sonipat section of the Northern Railway. The project aims to advance green rail mobility by reducing reliance on fossil fuel-based traction systems.

stories.title: Automotive industry focuses on sustainability leaders
stories.summary: The automotive industry is increasingly embedding sustainability into product development and manufacturing to meet regulatory and market pressures. Leaders are focusing on electric propulsion, supply chain transparency, and circularity strategies to connect environmental targets with commercial operations. The industry remains central to the global climate transition.

stories.title: UK offers £38 million for depot charging
stories.summary: The UK government has launched a £38 million funding scheme to help businesses install electric vehicle charging infrastructure at depots. The program covers up to 60 percent of installation costs for vans, trucks, and coaches. It is part of a wider £171 million effort to support commercial fleet electrification.

stories.title: HAM Group opens first LNG-CNG station in Mexico
stories.summary: HAM Group has opened its first liquefied and compressed natural gas refueling station in San Luis Potosi, Mexico. The facility is designed to support heavy-duty commercial transport and logistics corridors. The expansion comes as nearshoring activity drives higher freight volumes across the region.

stories.title: Tata Motors and Iveco Group form partnership
stories.summary: Tata Motors and Iveco Group have announced a new commercial mobility enterprise. The partnership combines industrial heritage and product portfolios to compete across global markets and technology cycles. The companies aim to leverage their combined scale and reach to grow within the international commercial vehicle sector.

research.title: CAFE: Closed-Loop Autonomous Task Formulation and Execution without Instance-Specific Instructions
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Scene-driven robot autonomy requires selecting tasks from observations as well as executing them. We study scene-driven task formulation and execution under predefined cleaning, safety, and storage/organization categories, without instance-specific goals or action sequences. CAFE maintains online. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Curie's Jarvis: Autonomous Robotic Chemistry Experiments from Printed Protocols
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: A person running a bench experiment works from a printed instruction sheet, tells identical containers apart by the labels written on them, and looks at the bench again before each step. Lab automation usually works the. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: DOBB: Dynamic Oriented Bounding Boxes for Multi-Agent Collision Avoidance under State Uncertainty and Heterogeneous Dynamics
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Learning-based decentralized collision avoidance must remain reliable under state-estimation uncertainty and heterogeneous agent dynamics. Existing methods typically address these factors through training-domain variation or by exposing uncertainty and capability estimates to the policy at runtime. However. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Data-Driven Robust Dynamic Wireless Charging Lane Planning with Tunable Profit--Risk Trade-off and Modified User Equilibrium
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Dynamic wireless charging (DWC) has attracted increasing attention as a complement to conventional plug-in charging for electric vehicles (EVs). However, existing planning methods for dynamic wireless charging lanes (DWCLs) overlook realistic EV routing and charging behavior. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Decision-Focused Learning via Neural Optimization Layers for Battery-Assisted Grid-Import Smoothing in AI Data Centers
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Rapid AI data-center power fluctuations challenge grid integration. Sustained grid-import smoothing requires allocating limited battery power and energy under uncertain demand. We formulate risk-aware BESS scheduling that coordinates advance reserve commitments and demand-responsive dispatch, accounting for. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Differentiable Filtering for Inertial Odometry
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate inertial odometry is critical for autonomous systems but suffers from unbounded drift caused by the integration of sensor noise and biases. In approaches such as TLIO, neural pseudo-measurements are trained independently of their downstream filter. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Incremental Input-to-State Stabilization of Partially Unknown Control-Affine Systems within Prescribed Safe Sets
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Incremental input-to-state stability ($\delta$-ISS) guarantees that the trajectories of a system converge towards one another, up to a gain on the difference of their inputs. Some existing learning-based designs that combine incremental stability with safety achieve. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Input-to-State Safety and Small-Gain Theorems for Large-Scale Nonlinear Systems
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies the safety verification problem for a general class of large-scale systems characterized by multiple safety indicator functions. Each safety indicator function satisfies a trajectory-based input-to-state safety (ISSf) estimate that provides a lower bound. Preprint, not peer reviewed.
